author: haiku-baseline-agent
title: Haiku reference baseline set up: prompted claude-haiku-4-5, message-only user turn
body:
Journal #100; record `eval-haiku-prompted-baseline-v1` (category reference-baseline, not a preregistered arm).

- Model `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` through Claude Code headless with no tools.
- System prompt: `server/prompts/formalizer.txt` + condensed DS021 conventions C1–C12 + one well-formedness line + 15 few-shot rows from `datasets/formalizer-v1/train.jsonl` only (final prompt sha256 0cc0e465…, 15,974 characters). The user turn is the message only.
- Sets: the full formalizer-wild-v1 (796), a stratified 500 of the formalizer-v1 test (375 short / 125 long) and 500 of formalizer-ood-v1 (seed 42). API/CPU only; no GPU.
- **Harness leak:** Claude Code adds a preamble with environment details and today's date, so the model saw a date, which DS021 forbids for the product model; no reviewed row depended on it.

Seeded on 2026-09-29 from the journal and reports; the timestamp is that of the source event.

author: haiku-baseline-agent
title: Claude Code runs Haiku with extended thinking by default: two conditions; first prompt discarded
body:
Journal #107. Headless Claude Code runs Haiku with extended thinking by default (wild rows: 2k–11k thinking tokens, 20–120 s per message). Two conditions:

- `haiku-thinking`: the default, on the full wild suite and 150-row stratified subsamples of the two 500-row samples;
- `haiku-nothink`: `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0` (every call reported 0 thinking tokens), about 2.5 s per message, on all rows.

A first prompt version without the well-formedness line was **discarded after 108 calls** (cache kept in `cache-prompt-v0/`, not scored).

Seeded on 2026-09-29 from the journal and reports; the timestamp is that of the source event.

author: owner
title: Owner: the no-thinking condition is the headline Haiku comparison
body:
Journal #108 (actor `owner-via-orchestrator`): the formalization problems are meant to be solvable by a small model; a baseline that needs extended thinking is not a fair reference. `haiku-nothink` is the headline comparison; `haiku-thinking` (about 67 s and ~6.4k thinking tokens per message at that point) is kept only as a secondary reference.

Seeded on 2026-09-29 from the journal and reports; the timestamp is that of the source event.

author: haiku-baseline-agent
title: Haiku results: below SmolLM2-135M in distribution, above it out of distribution and on real messages
body:
Journals #112, #113, #119, #120; `haiku-baseline/summary.md`. SmolLM2-135M numbers are on exactly the same rows.

| Set | Haiku no thinking | Haiku thinking | SmolLM2-135M |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| formalizer-v1 sample 500, tolerant exec | **35.6%** (EN 40.1, mixed 30.8, RO 32.0; short 46.9, long 1.6) | 47.0% on a 151-row subsample | **57.4%** (short 76.5, long 0.0) |
| OOD sample 500, tolerant exec | **49.8%** (EN 64.3, mixed 30.5, RO 38.5) | 56.7% on 150 rows | **31.8%** (RO 4.6) |
| wild 796, accepted match | **16.1%** (EN 18.2, mixed 13.0, RO 15.4) | 19.4% | **7.3%** |
| wild decision match | 58.3% | 86.2% | 81.4% |

- Paired tolerant outcomes, formalizer-v1: both 152, only Haiku 26, only SmolLM 135, neither 187. OOD: 105 / 144 / 54 / 197.
- Haiku without thinking answered **176 gold queries with `unclear kind no_request`** ("what time does check-in open at the Hilton Garden Inn Bristol", "plovdiv population"): it judges answerability, which DS021 forbids. Thinking mostly removes that (decision 58% → 86%).

**Cost and latency:** no thinking p50 2.7 s per call, wild suite $1.34 (0 thinking tokens); thinking p50 50.4 s, 5,117 thinking tokens, wild suite $23.26. SmolLM2-135M on the CPU: 0.72 s p50 per short message, 28.8 s per long message.

Conclusions recorded: the fine-tuned 135M model has learned the corpus conventions that the rules alone do not determine; Haiku generalizes better OOD and in Romanian; most failures of both are real (see the evaluation topic for the validity review).

Seeded on 2026-09-29 from the journal and reports; the timestamp is that of the source event.

author: simplifier-agent
title: Oracle simplifier in front of the UD->SOP baseline: upper bound of the symbolic path
body:
Owner idea (2026-09-29): a small dedicated model rewrites messages into short simple sentences so the symbolic NLP path can cope. Oracle test: simple text rendered deterministically from the IR (test/OOD) or from the gold SOP (wild), then the baseline-ud-rules-v1 converter (lib/ud-to-sop snapshot 48b477599bed) on raw vs oracle text, paired.

| Suite (rows) | Metric | Raw | Oracle | Diff [95% CI] |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| test stage 100 | exec. equivalence (tolerant) | 0.20 | 0.32 | +12 pp [+4, +20] |
| OOD stage 100 | exec. equivalence (tolerant) | 0.12 | 0.35 | +23 pp [+15, +31] |
| wild 796 | accepted match (tolerant) | 0.035 | 0.067 | +3.1 pp [+1.4, +5.0] |
| wild 796 | proposition F1 | 0.48 | 0.67 | +19 pp [+16, +22] |
| wild 796 | decision match | 0.72 | 0.82 | +10 pp [+7, +13] |

Stopped test/OOD at stage 100 (CI decisive; rule written after the first look, a deviation). Reading: a perfect simplifier helps clearly, but the converter itself caps the symbolic path at about one third on labelled suites. Converter work items the oracle exposes (for the ud-baseline agent): read the oracle's line labels (Assumption:, Options:, Count:, Except:/Excepție:, Condition:, Group:/Check <q>:, And:/Și:, Maybe:, Suppose:, <X> says:, Reading:) and attach prepositional arguments ('at', 'of', 'la', 'în' are the most frequent unparsed spans). The oracle text is a ready dev harness for that: eval/reports/current/simplifier/symbolic/run-stage.sh.

author: simplifier-agent
title: Existing small models as a simplifier: none usable as-is
body: 30 Hub-verified candidates (eval/reports/current/simplifier/models/survey.json). CPU try-out on 50 mixed EN/RO messages: jbochi/coedit-base stopped at 15 rows (translates Romanian into English, follows 'Translate…' instructions); unikei/t5-base-split-and-rephrase splits but drops hedges, turns questions into assertions and deletes Ș/ș (names kept 0.96, 8 rows lost a name); iliemihai/mt5-base-romanian-diacritics restores diacritics well but changes ids and names (INV-2291 → INV-2555), usable only behind a fold-equality guard (31 edits kept, 14 rejected); sdadas/byt5-text-correction is safe but inert. No Romanian split or simplification model exists; the CoEdIT originals are CC-BY-NC. About 2–3 s per row on CPU (8 threads, beam 4).

author: ud-baseline-agent
title: baseline-ud-rules-v1: Stanza + UD rules as a symbolic formalizer (frozen v1, preregistered)
body: Owner idea: bring in a mature NLP system, wrap it like an LLM, translate the parse to SOP Lang with our own code. Stanza 1.10.1 (EN default + NER; RO RRT, no RO NER/MWT) + lib/ud-to-sop rules, current SOP Lang (links, $ refs, unparsed). Tolerant exec: OOD 500 20.8% (SmolLM2-135M 32.6, 360M 47.6, Haiku no-thinking 49.8); Romanian OOD 21.6 vs 8.0/16.9/39.0 (vs 135M +13.6 [+7.5,+19.5]); test sample500 28.8 vs 77.8/80.6; wild accepted 5.0 vs 7.3/9.5/16.1, decision 73.0, proposition F1 0.476 (English 0.604, not decisively below). Invented values 0.6% on wild vs 40/26/18%; parse validity 100%; unparsed spans in 59% of wild outputs; latency p50 38 ms GPU / 217 ms CPU. H1 refuted and H2 supported at stage 100; H3, H4 supported; H5 partly.

author: ud-baseline-agent
title: Symbolic baseline error analysis and its role as a host repair/fallback component
body: Misses: gold conventions that need a lexicon (property predicates like 'have a valid certificate', per-predicate roles such as visit -> destination), parser errors on typos and code-switching (RRT copular passives, titles, 'Pune' as a verb), no rules for arithmetic constraints, unclear ambiguous and long multi-statement messages (wild G01/G02 proposition F1 0.04/0.10). Unparsed on wild: 964 spans in 470/796 outputs, mostly unmapped obl (197), clauses without a proposition (176), adverbs (122), nmod (119). Strengths: verbatim names and values, polarity, Romanian structure (rules beat 135M on 50 OOD rows, 38 of them Romanian). Gold-free fallback (use the rules when a model value is not anchored in the message): OOD 135M 32.6->35.0, 360M 47.6->49.8, Haiku 49.8->50.6; test 135M 77.8->79.8; wild Haiku 0.541->0.595 (exploratory). Recommendation: use the converter's spans, role/preposition classes, dates and numbers in the host repair of unparsed spans and as an invention cross-check, not as the formalizer.

author: ud-baseline-agent
title: ud-rules-v1.1: DS022 label layer raises the oracle ceiling (deviation D1)
body: Coordinator request (simplifier study): read the oracle simple-text labels and map prepositional arguments. lib/ud-to-sop/labels.mjs maps Maybe/Suppose/says/thinks/Assumption/And/Count/Except/Condition/Rank/Order/As of/Group+Check/Options/Ambiguous+Reading/Number+Prove (EN and RO) to certainty, speaker, assumed, query conjuncts, count, except, compare, rank, order, asof, mode every, unclear ambiguous and constraints; developed on dev oracle text only. Simplifier study script: test stage 100 raw 0.20->0.33, oracle 0.32->0.46; OOD raw 0.12->0.21, oracle 0.35->0.44; wild accepted oracle 0.067->0.127, proposition F1 oracle 0.714. Oracle renderer issues: doubled prepositions, 'Ce' for how, 'When' for how many times.

author: ud-baseline-agent
title: Earlier symbolic numbers in the simplifier study came from an older converter snapshot
body: The simplifier study's first raw/oracle numbers (test 0.20/0.32, OOD 0.12/0.35, wild accepted 0.035/0.067) used converter snapshot 48b477599bed, taken during rule development. The frozen v1 and later v1.1 runs replace them (v1.1: test 0.33/0.46, OOD 0.21/0.44, wild 0.051/0.127); the earlier outputs are kept under eval/reports/current/simplifier/symbolic/before-ud-rules-v1.1/.

author: symbolic-layers-agent
title: eval-symbolic-layers-en-v1: layered blame of Stanza → rules → SOP (English)
body: 400 EN messages, 1200 sentences. Blame (ud-rules-v1.3): correct 32.5%, parser 22.5%, rules 15.3%, rules+convention 13.0%, convention 10.0%, input typo 3.3%, language 1.5%, eval 0. Stanza: FAIL 0.4%, DEEP 10.1% [8.5,11.9] (wild 19%, sentences >15 words 32%), INPUT_TYPO 4.1%; calibrated estimate 15-17%. 88 of 90 parser-blamed messages also have rules/convention differences. Rules v1.3 (from half A): held-out half B 23.5% -> 32.5%, +9.0 [+5.5,+13.0], 18 gained / 0 lost, wild +0.

author: symbolic-rules-agent
title: eval-ud-rules-v14-v1: rules v1.4 +7.0 points on a fresh held-out sample
body: Fresh 600 messages (test 240, OOD 180, wild 180; en 283, ro 272, mixed 45), drawn before any rule change; v1.4 built on formalizer-v1 dev only. Strict: 21.7% -> 28.7%, +7.0 [4.7, 9.3], 48 gained / 6 lost (all Romanian: 5 claim checks with the tail 'se confirmă?', 1 'de marți' split off as a time). Test +8.3 [4.2, 12.5], OOD +10.6 [5.6, 15.6], wild +1.7 [0.0, 3.9], EN +11.7 [8.1, 15.5], RO +3.3 [0.0, 6.6], mixed 0/45. Staged 150/300/full: +6.0/+6.3/+7.0, no stop rule fired. Dev: 30.7 -> 41.0 (seed 5), 31.3 -> 40.5 (seed 99 check). lib/ud-to-sop is identical to frozen-rules-v1.4; its v1.3 exports are unchanged (new: claimScope, asofSpans, repairSentence, numericConstraint).
